messages.content: Add the assignee to the Board settings

Profile slector must be used in single selection only and update the "assignee" field in the board.
 Kanban store must update the assignee field and save.
Board views must show the assignee profile if present.

I'll explore the current implementation of the board settings modal, the kanban store, and the profile selector.Let me look at the kanban store and the modals directly.Now I'll implement the changes. Starting with the profile selector (single-selection support) and the avatar fallback.Now the kanban store — persisting the board `assignee` field and resolving it for the views.Now the board settings modal — the profile selector switches to single selection bound to the board `assignee`.Now the board views — showing the assignee profile in the kanban and sprint headers.The board settings modal has one stray character in a comment — fixing it.One last polish pass on the modal: the selector trigger should keep a stable "Assignee" label.Implementation complete. Summary of what changed and why:

## 1. Single-selection profile picker
`src/components/chat/ChatProfileSelector.vue`
- New props: `single`, `allow-deselect`, plus `label` / `icon` / `empty-label` overrides (defaults unchanged, so every existing usage keeps multi-select behaviour).
- New `select` event carrying **one** profile name (or `null` when cleared). Multi-select callers are untouched.

## 2. Board settings → `assignee` (one profile)
`src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue`
- The old multi-select "Assignees (profiles)" block became **Assignee** bound to `editBoardForm.assignee` (a single profile **name**), using `ChatProfileSelector` with `single` + `allow-deselect`, `label="Assignee"`, `empty-label="No assignee"`, plus a removable chip for one-click clearing.
- `DEFAULT_EDIT_BOARD` → `assignee: null` (was `profiles: []`); `openEditBoard` prefills `board.assignee`; `confirmEditBoard` emits `assignee` on `board-updated`.
- New computed `editBoardAssignee` resolves the stored name back into the one-item list the picker understands (falls back to `{ name }`).
- Column profiles keep their multi-select (they are a different, legitimately multi-valued field).

## 3. Kanban store persists and resolves the assignee
`src/store/kanban.js`
- `normalizeAssignee()` — blank values become `null` (never `''`).
- `saveBoard` now writes `assignee` (omitted ⇒ keep stored, empty ⇒ clear) and still saves the board; `addBoard` accepts `assignee`.
- `storedBoards` exposes a stable `assignee` (virtual board: `null`).
- New getter `boardAssignee(boardId)` → resolves the profile name against **the board's own project** (`$state.profiles` / `profilesByProject`), with a `{ name }` fallback so the header never breaks.
- `exportBoard` / `importBoard` carry `assignee` so transferred/copied boards keep it.

## 4. Board views show the assignee
- `src/components/kanban/board/KanbanBoardView.vue` — `ProfileAvatar` in the board top bar next to the board title (`boardAssignee` computed).
- `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardView.vue` — `ProfileAvatar` + name chip in the sprint toolbar (`assigneeProfile` computed).
- `src/components/profile/ProfileAvatar.vue` — gravatar/robohash fallback (same as `ProfileCard`) + `alt`, so an assignee whose profile is still loading never renders a broken image.

Flow: Board settings → pick one profile → `board.assignee` (name) → store `saveBoard` → kanban document → both board headers render the resolved profile.
